analysis.title: Wayfair Inc. (W) Q3'26 Review: Share Gains Broaden as Customer Growth & Advertising Efficiency Improve
key_insights: Wayfair's Q3'26 net revenue ($3,420mm) and adjusted EBITDA ($236mm) beat GS ($3,396mm / $223mm) and consensus ($3,369mm / $223mm). US revenue grew +11.4% YoY, with orders delivered +12.2% YoY.

Active customers grew +4.7% YoY to 22.2mm (LTM). Management credits stores, loyalty and customer experience improvements. The company is gaining share in a home category that GS describes as roughly flat.
Management said its US share spread has reached double digits and sees room for further expansion into 2027.

Advertising is showing leverage, supported by better repeat behavior, the Rewards loyalty program and a shift toward direct traffic. Management says Rewards drives higher customer spend, broader cross-category engagement and lower reacquisition costs.
Physical retail: Atlanta and Columbus show early market-level lifts similar to Chicago. Five additional stores are expected to open in 2027.
Agentic commerce: AI-referred traffic more than doubled sequentially to about 1% of total traffic, and Wayfair is expanding partnerships.

Negatives: international revenue fell -2.3% YoY, Q3 AOV fell -2% YoY on mix shift, and management expects Q4 gross margin at the low end of the 29.5%-30.5% guided range because of strategic investment and loyalty program pressure.

GS expects investor debate to center on sustainability of share gains, durability of advertising leverage, the trade-off between gross margin reinvestment and acquisition efficiency, and the pace of retail investment in 2027.
GS reiterates Neutral, raises 12-month PT to $116 from $102 (price $111.32, 4.2% upside). The PT blends 22.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA on NTM+1 and 31.0x EV/FCF-SBC on NTM+4 discounted 3 years at 12%.

Estimate changes: Q4'26 revenue $3.65bn (from $3.56bn), adj. EBITDA $237mm (from $245mm), GAAP EPS $0.37 (from $0.27). 2027 revenue $14.62bn (from $14.35bn), adj. EBITDA $1.02bn (unchanged), GAAP EPS $1.69 (from $1.50).

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Neutral and raises PT from $102 to $116 after a Q3'26 beat and higher estimates. The stock is at $111.32, 4.2% below target.

sector_views.rationale: The home category remains roughly flat and near the bottom of the cycle. GS sees Wayfair taking share as transaction volume shifts toward online and omnichannel.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported 11/4/26 (GS note): net revenue $3,420mm vs GS $3,396mm and consensus $3,369mm. Adj. EBITDA $236mm vs GS $223mm and consensus $223mm. Adj. EBITDA margin 7%, about +33bps vs GS and +28bps vs consensus.
Q3'26 actuals: LTM active customers 22.2mm vs consensus 21.7mm, orders delivered 11.0mm vs consensus 10.46mm, net revenue per customer $596 vs consensus $605, orders per customer 1.9 in line.

Q4'26 GS estimates (new vs old): revenue $3,646mm (from $3,565mm), adj. EBITDA $237mm (from $245mm), adj. EBITDA margin 6.5% (from 6.9%), GAAP EPS $0.37 (from $0.27). Management expects Q4 gross margin at the low end of 29.5%-30.5%.

GS FY26E revenue $13,516mm (from $13,411mm), adj. EBITDA $866mm (from $862mm). FY27E revenue $14,621mm (from $14,348mm), adj. EBITDA $1,024mm (from $1,019mm), GAAP EPS $1.69 (from $1.50). FY28E revenue $15,762mm, adj. EBITDA $1,200mm.
risk_factors: Discretionary consumer budgets and demand for online furniture.
Ramp of strategic initiatives (advertising, logistics) affecting gross profit trajectory.
Seller relationships affecting selection and pricing.
Dual-class share structure with concentrated voting power.
Gross margin pressure from loyalty program investment.
International weakness in Canada and the UK.
Upside risk: any sign of a return to sustained positive revenue growth in the category.

tension_points.bull_case: Orders and customer growth are accelerating, repeat behavior and advertising efficiency are improving, and the US share spread has reached double digits with room to expand into 2027. GS sees structural drivers behind the topline.
tension_points.bear_case: The home category is still near the bottom of the cycle. Gross margin is under pressure from loyalty reinvestment, AOV fell -2% YoY, international revenue is declining, and investors may question the durability of advertising leverage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Any sign the advertising leverage fades or gross margin reinvestment outweighs acquisition efficiencies. GS names no specific level.

theme_stances.key_argument: Accelerating orders and customer growth, stronger repeat behavior and better acquisition efficiency give share gains a more durable foundation.
theme_stances.evidence: Wayfair's improving topline trajectory is increasingly being driven by structural factors
